name: jsvine/waybackpack

name: traffic

No large committed dataset, but a well-documented, actively used client that dramatically eases historical OpenSky state-vector pulls.
why_useful: If the team wants to nowcast global or route-level flight volumes from OpenSky's historical Impala database (deeper history and finer grain than the pre-built COVID-19 CSV dumps), this is the standard tool academics use to do it -- lowers the acquisition cost for gap #10.

name: dbnomics/rdbnomics

name: nowcast_lstm

No datasets committed but ships an example notebook+data zip. 90 commits, MIT, v0.2.6, sibling R/Julia/MATLAB wrappers exist (nowcastLSTM, NowcastLSTM.jl, nowcast_lstm_matlab). Built by a UNCTAD staffer for official nowcasting use.

name: nowcastDFM

why_useful: Alternative DFM toolkit to FRBNY's MATLAB code, in R, with an explicit feature for decomposing how each new weekly data point moves the nowcast -- useful if building a homegrown weekly ABNB-demand tracker (gap #17).

what_it_holds: MATLAB package with fred.latest(series) and fred.vint(series, vintage_date) for pulling FRED/ALFRED data at a specific vintage date, including a 'pseudo-vintage' mode that simulates publication lag for series without full ALFRED vintage history, plus parallelized bulk downloads across many series/vintage dates.
why_useful: Same ALFRED vintage capability as fredapi but for MATLAB users, and notably adds simulated publication-delay handling for series that lack full vintage archives -- useful if the team needs point-in-time treatment of a FRED series ALFRED doesn't fully vintage.
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: Same ALFRED vintage capability as fredapi but for MATLAB users, and notably adds simulated publication-delay handling for series that lack full vintage archives -- useful if the team needs point-in-time treatment of a FRED series ALFRED doesn't fully vintage.

name: macro-dashboard (zero-cost US macro forecasting engine)
what_it_holds: Vintage-true backtesting harness pulling 84 FRED series + full ALFRED vintages (~3,800 API calls for a full backtest) + BLS CPI/employment + Yahoo Finance gold, with release-date filtering, real ALFRED vintages, and expanding (not full-sample) z-scores to close look-ahead leak channels; validated over 147 quarterly as-of dates since 1990, 695 scored points, 0 leaks. No data files are committed -- everything is pulled live via tools/backfill.py.
why_useful: This is close to a working template for exactly the 'vintage-aware backtest' methodology gap #17/#4 calls for -- release-date filtering + real vintages + expanding-window normalization is the standard fix for the leakage problems the repo's own backtests must avoid.
